title: Grammar: The Verb 'Tener'
description: Deep practice of 'tener': age, possessions, feelings, and the 'tener que' structure.

sentences.spanish: Tengo veinticinco años.
sentences.english: I am twenty-five years old.

sentences.spanish: Mi hermana tiene diez años.
sentences.english: My sister is ten years old.

sentences.spanish: ¿Cuántos años tienes tú?
sentences.english: How old are you?

sentences.spanish: Tengo dos hermanos y una hermana.
sentences.english: I have two brothers and one sister.

sentences.spanish: ¿Tienes animales en casa?
sentences.english: Do you have pets at home?

sentences.spanish: Tenemos un piso pequeño en el centro.
sentences.english: We have a small flat in the city centre.

sentences.spanish: Vosotros tenéis mucha suerte.
sentences.english: You all are very lucky.

sentences.spanish: Mis padres tienen una casa en la costa.
sentences.english: My parents have a house on the coast.

sentences.spanish: Ella tiene mucho talento para la música.
sentences.english: She has a great talent for music.

sentences.spanish: Tengo hambre, ¿comemos algo?
sentences.english: I'm hungry, shall we eat something?

sentences.spanish: ¿Tienes sed? Hay zumo en la nevera.
sentences.english: Are you thirsty? There's juice in the fridge.

sentences.spanish: El bebé tiene sueño.
sentences.english: The baby is sleepy.

sentences.spanish: Tengo frío, voy a ponerme un jersey.
sentences.english: I'm cold, I'm going to put on a jumper.

sentences.spanish: En verano tenemos mucho calor aquí.
sentences.english: In summer we're really hot here.

sentences.spanish: Tengo miedo de las arañas.
sentences.english: I'm afraid of spiders.

sentences.spanish: Creo que tienes razón.
sentences.english: I think you're right.

sentences.spanish: Perdona, tengo prisa, ¿lo dejamos para mañana?
sentences.english: Sorry, I'm in a hurry, shall we leave it for tomorrow?

sentences.spanish: Tengo muchas ganas de ir a la playa.
sentences.english: I really feel like going to the beach.

sentences.spanish: ¿Tienes ganas de probar mi tortilla de patatas?
sentences.english: Do you fancy trying my Spanish omelette?

sentences.spanish: Tengo que estudiar para el examen.
sentences.english: I have to study for the exam.

sentences.spanish: Mañana tengo que madrugar.
sentences.english: Tomorrow I have to get up early.

sentences.spanish: ¿Tienes que trabajar este sábado?
sentences.english: Do you have to work this Saturday?

sentences.spanish: Tenemos que hablar.
sentences.english: We need to talk.

sentences.spanish: Los niños tienen que recoger la habitación.
sentences.english: The children have to tidy their room.

sentences.spanish: Tengo que ir al médico porque me duele la cabeza.
sentences.english: I have to go to the doctor because my head hurts.

sentences.spanish: No tengo ni idea.
sentences.english: I haven't got a clue.

sentences.spanish: Tengo tu móvil en mi bolsillo.
sentences.english: I've got your mobile in my pocket.

sentences.spanish: ¿Tenéis planes para el fin de semana?
sentences.english: Have you all got plans for the weekend?

sentences.spanish: Mis abuelos tienen ochenta y dos años.
sentences.english: My grandparents are eighty-two years old.

sentences.spanish: Tenemos tiempo de tomar algo antes del cine.
sentences.english: We have time for a quick drink before the cinema.

grammarExplanation:
'Tener' means 'to have', but Spanish uses it where English uses 'to be':

• Age → Tengo veinticinco años = I AM twenty-five
• Feelings → tener hambre (hungry), sed (thirsty), frío (cold), calor (hot), sueño (sleepy), miedo (afraid), prisa (in a hurry)
• Opinion → tener razón = to be right
• Desire → tener ganas de + infinitive = to feel like doing something
• Obligation → tener que + infinitive = to have to do something

Conjugation:
• Tengo = I have
• Tienes = you have
• Tiene = he/she has
• Tenemos = we have
• Tenéis = you all have (Spain)
• Tienen = they have

suerte.explanation: Luck. Tener suerte = to be lucky.

razón.explanation: Reason. Tener razón = to be right.

ganas.explanation: Urge / desire. Tener ganas de + infinitive = to feel like doing something.

prisa.explanation: Hurry. Tener prisa = to be in a hurry.
